exam.title: Databricks Certified Generative AI Engineer Associate
exam.study_prerequisites: No formal prerequisite; the official guide recommends related training and six months of hands-on experience. Practice Python/SQL, prompt and model selection, governed document preparation, RAG and AI Search, traced agent/tool/MCP design, MLflow evaluation, secure Apps/serving, Unity Catalog controls, CI/CD, monitoring, cost control and calibrated feedback.

review.notes: The March 18, 2026 detailed live-version PDF and current six-domain weighted page were reconciled, with live assessment metadata controlling PDF delivery discrepancies. Three scenarios, eight labs and 37 original checks cover requirement/prompt/task/chain/tool and Agent Bricks choices; governed extraction, chunking, embeddings, AI Search/Vector Search, retrieval metrics and reranking; model/framework selection, layered guardrails, Agent Framework and Genie/multi-agent behavior; packaging/registration, Foundation Model/batch inference, memory, CI/CD, prompt lifecycle, MCP and secure Apps; Unity Catalog/masking/licensing controls; and traced evaluation, judges/scorers, inference/usage/cost monitoring and calibrated SME feedback. All 12 guide URLs are cataloged: 9 reachable, with the two Udemy pages and O'Reilly search automation-blocked; none missing or broken. Fast-moving Agent Bricks, MCP, Apps, AI Search, MLflow and AI Gateway names/release stages are explicitly volatile, and vendor sample questions are linked rather than reproduced.

findings.title: AI Search permissions were too broadly described
findings.evidence: AI Search explicitly lacks row/column permissions despite source-table governance.
findings.recommendation: Explain trusted application filtering or scoped indexes, bypass prevention, and per-hop checks.
findings.resolution: Explain trusted application filtering or scoped indexes, bypass prevention, and per-hop checks.

findings.title: UI authentication did not prove user-delegated resource access
findings.evidence: An App service principal has shared grants; user authorization requires supported scopes and use of delegated identity.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit identity example and distinguish delegated SQL policies from AI Search limits.
findings.resolution: Add explicit identity example and distinguish delegated SQL policies from AI Search limits.

findings.title: Completed evaluation did not imply complete scoring
findings.evidence: Current scorer reference permits continuing after exceptions. Local MLflow confirmed mean 1.0 with one error among three rows.
findings.recommendation: Require attempted/scored/error coverage and an incomplete release gate; explain offline expectations and subclass limits.
findings.resolution: Require attempted/scored/error coverage and an incomplete release gate; explain offline expectations and subclass limits.

findings.title: Retrieval and PyFunc objectives lacked executable worked examples
findings.evidence: Recall and hit rate were paired without a denominator example; PyFunc chain coding was only described.
findings.recommendation: Add two original executable examples, four decision cases and twelve answered checks.
findings.resolution: Add two original executable examples, four decision cases and twelve answered checks.

findings.title: Raw monitor change needed semantic interpretation
findings.evidence: Domain snapshot changed hyphens to en-dashes and previous status snapshot is absent. Normalized six-domain text is equal.
findings.recommendation: Record observed status and formatting difference without claiming a new blueprint or silently changing accepted snapshots.
findings.resolution: Record observed status and formatting difference without claiming a new blueprint or silently changing accepted snapshots.

blog_intake.value: Controlled code-corpus chunking comparisons and trace-level answer completeness; disambiguation metadata matters.
blog_intake.limits: Workload-specific findings; varying actual chunk sizes and judge model are confounders, not universal splitter performance.
